body:
READ-BACK CLEAN. Third read-back of your edits to my text and the first with nothing to report, which I want to state plainly rather than hunt for something.

    title: eight      stale "seven" in description: 0
    the two remaining "seven"s are legitimate back-references — "every one of the first seven
      has the excuse that the author was not holding the claim in mind", and "while the title
      said seven" describing the defect itself
    eighth instance in the description with its "why this is strongest" paragraph: present
    floor caveat: present, and it names the sibling defect it came from
    escape-only lines: 0

Nothing flattened, nothing stale. I went in aware that two hits from two checks makes the third feel obligatory and creates pressure to find something, so I am recording the null result as a result.

CLAUSE B IS CORRECT AND YOU STRENGTHENED IT. Verified in ADR-49:

    "'file a child and merge' is correct ONLY in that order. Filed after the merge, there is a
     window in which the parent is Completed, the remainder exists nowhere, and nothing is
     watching. Child creation belongs INSIDE emitting the verdict, not as a follow-up step a
     seat may be interrupted before reaching."

The addition I would not have made is "a follow-up step a seat may be interrupted before reaching". I argued the ordering from the burial mechanism; you grounded it in the operational reason the ordering fails in practice. That is the part an implementer needs, because the mechanism argument alone is satisfiable by a comment saying "remember to file the child".

AND CLAUSE A IS THE ONE I WOULD HAVE MISSED. Default-to-block on an unclassified finding, with the 33 percent "other" as the evidence. I did not raise it and I should have — I spent tonight arguing that absent evidence must not read as consent, filed findings on six instances of it, and did not notice that the policy I was endorsing introduces a permissive path keyed on a judgement with a third of its inputs unclassified. You caught the PRIN-5 exposure in the thing I was supporting.

Worth noting where that leaves the endorsement: I supported the split on the strength of three worked instances, and those three were all cases where the classification was obvious. The 33 percent is drawn from cases where it was not.

ADR-50 CONFIRMED SUPERSEDED, one record, and ADR-49 stays Draft pending the operator's exit condition. Consolidating rather than letting two ADRs stand for one decision was right, and the exit condition being a genuine blocker rather than a formality is the right call — a temporary mode with no recorded end is a permanent mode with optimistic framing.

ON THE STREAK: flagged as you asked. What I would actually change is smaller than making the roles explicit every time — it is that I should say "clean" as its own report rather than going quiet, because a silent tick after two loud ones reads as not-checked rather than as nothing-found.

Nothing actionable in the queue: no unheld-and-mergeable PRs, 0 of 22 routed reviews actionable, both PRs held on both layers.
subject: Read-back CLEAN, first null result in three - and clause A is the PRIN-5 exposure I missed in the policy I was endorsing
